title: Dynamic colony history reveals limits of static island architecture for predicting temporal demographic coupling in Antarctic penguins

already_established: Pygoscelid colony size and distribution have been tested against neighbouring colony abundance, distance and foraging-range competition since at least Ainley et al. 1995.
Antarctic-wide colony size, clustering and distribution have been related to social neighbourhoods, breeding-habitat availability, polynyas and submarine canyons (Santora et al. 2020).
Strong synchrony in annual Adélie colony growth has been documented in the Ross Sea (Lyver et al. 2014).
Range-wide multiscale work has shown that prevailing sea ice can predict multidecadal Adélie growth while annual sea-ice anomalies explain little annual growth variance (Iles et al. 2020).
not_novel_here: that Antarctic penguin colony geography is structured
that physical breeding habitat can matter
that social neighbourhoods and density dependence can affect colony distribution or size
that penguin colonies can fluctuate synchronously
that environmental predictors can explain multidecadal population trends
new_precedent_boundary.part_II_target_novelty: A predeclared cross-species test of whether static terrestrial breeding-landscape traits predict site-specific coupling of long-term local time series to annual demographic variation shared within each Pygoscelis species.
new_precedent_boundary.response_boundary: Earlier geographic studies primarily analyze colony occurrence, size, spacing or clustering; Part II analyzes temporal coupling/loadings estimated from long-term abundance time series. These responses are not interchangeable.

writing_rules: Explicitly acknowledge prior Antarctic work on colony size/distribution and social/physical geographic structure before stating Part II novelty.
Explicitly acknowledge prior Ross Sea annual synchrony and range-wide multiscale sea-ice demography.
State that Part II tests temporal demographic coupling rather than colony size, distribution, spacing or clustering.
Do not imply that the Part II non-confirmatory result contradicts evidence that geography or environment structures Antarctic penguin populations.
Scope the title and Abstract to temporal demographic coupling rather than Antarctic penguin demography in general.
Retain every v0.4 public-information novelty boundary and all frozen numerical decisions.
No Ross unpublished behavioral result may enter the evidentiary manuscript.
prohibited_language: first Antarctic-wide test of penguin geography
static geography does not predict penguin demography
